competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both descriptions the competency names are explicitly enacted rather than implied: counting up appears as starting at a number and counting on, and putting together appears verbatim in the group-combining items, with a part-whole item asking for the sum of two stated parts.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The variety of models clause is genuinely met - a number line to move along, pictured rows of books and trees to combine, and an abstract two-part frame - and the addition is approached both as an increment of one and as a join of two sizeable groups.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Single-step joins with no regrouping language, plus short check-my-work items naming a pupil and a proposed answer, keep the reasoning at one operation, which suits Quarter 1; the emoji rows keep the pictorial model literally countable.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Seven different response formats appear across the sixteen samples, including an error-detection item and a verdict on a stated total, so the pupil encounters addition as something to perform, to illustrate, and to check.

competency_alignment.rationale: All four true-or-false samples key to False, so that slice can be swept without adding anything - and the generator demonstrably can vary a verdict, since the error-detection pair splits, with one item flagging an incorrect claim and another confirming a correct one. The decoys elsewhere also lean on a fixed decade-shift pattern, offering 29 beside 19 and 25 beside 15, which repeats one misconception rather than sampling several.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Sums run up to exactly 20 - the pictured item joining two rows of ten reaches the ceiling - and no sample crosses it, while addends stay small enough to count on from.
